items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: I’d been playing with Lou and I knew the kind of stuff he liked to hear

ctx.x: Yeah, a little higher up. Talk about learning on the job, that’s great. Well okay and you did that for a while and you came back here. How do you get, how did the channels open up for you that eventually got you to the next level up?

Well after I left Jimmy Cavallo’s band, the bass player and I actually left together and formed a trio, and we picked up a drummer in Atlantic City where we were working, his name was Jack Toker, a wonderful drummer. And Jack and I and the bass player had a © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-

group for about six months and that fell apart and I said okay, I decided I was going to come home, and the drummer said he was going to stay out on the road. Well he hooked up with a show band at that time, and this must have been ’69, ’70, right around that time. There were lots of gigs and so you could play the Holiday Inn circuit, you could keep working, again, covering songs on the radio, this stuff.
